quotes.quote: Following a quality check of the WGS data with the FastQC tool ( FastQC, A, 2015 ), the genomes were assembled using Shovill ver. 1.0.4 ( https://github.com/tseemann/shovill ), and a species check was performed using Kraken2 ( https://ccb.jhu.edu/software/kraken/ ).

AMR genes were identified via the Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI) ( https://card.mcmaster.ca/analyze/rgi ), while virulence genes were identified via the use of virulence factors of pathogenic bacteria (VFDB) ( http://www.mgc.ac.cn/VFs/ ) from the genome.

G1.rationale: The principal results (serotype, ST, AMR genes) are produced by computational analysis of WGS data that a third party can re-run from the deposited raw reads.

quotes.quote: One of the CIFT-K6 isolates had the uncommon serotype of K. pneumoniae O3b with the high-risk clone “ST37.”

Multiple locus sequence typing (MLST) using the WGS data revealed that two of the four genomes belonged to ST515, that of the CTFT-K6 isolate was typed as ST37, and that of the fourth isolate, CIFT-K10, was of the ST192 type.

G2.rationale: The paper's stated priority is the identification of serotype O3b and high-risk clone ST37; the principal quantitative result is the sequence type assignment (ST37) for isolate CIFT-K6.

quotes.quote: The whole genome project has been submitted as a project with the accession ID PRJNA704514. The whole-genome shotgun project has been deposited in DDBJ/ENA/GenBank under the accession numbers JAGIZC000000000 (CIFT-K6), JAGIZD000000000 (CIFT-K7), JAGIZE000000000 (CIFT-K8), and JAGIZF000000000 (CIFT-K10).

G3.rationale: The deposit listing contains raw sequencing reads (SRR accessions) under PRJNA704514, which are the analysis inputs for the computational target.

quotes.quote: Additional virulence plasmid-associated K loci (capsule synthesis) and O antigen (lipopolysaccharide) serotype prediction, allele diversity, and multiple locus sequence type (MLST) of K. pneumoniae were screened using KleBorate ( https://github.com/katholt/Kleborate ).

Following a quality check of the WGS data with the FastQC tool ( FastQC, A, 2015 ), the genomes were assembled using Shovill ver. 1.0.4 ( https://github.com/tseemann/shovill ), and a species check was performed using Kraken2 ( https://ccb.jhu.edu/software/kraken/ ).

G4.rationale: The method for MLST and serotype prediction is described with specific software (Kleborate) and version, sufficient to implement without original code.

leakage_files.name: SRR13775208
leakage_files.reason: This is raw sequencing data for one of the isolates; it does not contain the target value directly, but it is the input for the computation. However, if the target value is derived from it, it is not a leakage file. The leakage files are those that contain the target value or derived result tables. In this deposit listing, there are no such files; all are raw data. Therefore, leakage_files is empty.

specification.comparison_metric: The observed sequence type (ST) from re-running the analysis on the deposited raw reads is compared to the reported ST37 for isolate CIFT-K6.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Exact match of the sequence type string (ST37).
specification.specification_gaps: The mapping of SRR accessions to isolate names (CIFT-K6, etc.) is not provided. The version of Kleborate and the MLST database used are not specified. The exact parameters for assembly and annotation are not fully detailed.

alternatives_considered.reason: The paper's title highlights both serotype O3b and ST37, but ST37 is the high-risk clone and is more central to the conclusion. Serotype O3b is also reported, but the sequence type is the principal quantitative result for the high-risk clone identification.
This is a count, but it is a secondary result and not the principal target emphasized in the abstract and conclusion.
